The repository has no separate asynchronous method-view class, so the question's premise doesn't hold. I found no `async def` and no `Async*` view class in `src/quill/views.py`. Only `typing.py` mentions async types, and `app.py` has the async adapter described below.

**What exists in `src/quill/views.py`:**
- `Page` (L16-135) is the base class-based view. It defines `route_inquiry`, `to_page`, `methods`, `decorators` and `init_every_request`.
- `VerbPage(Page)` (L138-191) is the HTTP-method-dispatch view, the Flask `MethodView` equivalent. Its `__init_subclass__` builds `methods` from the lowercase verb handlers. Its `route_inquiry` looks up `getattr(self, request.method.lower())`, with HEAD falling back to `get`.

**How async is handled instead:**
- Async support is not a subclass. Both `Page.to_page` (L110, L116) and `VerbPage.route_inquiry` (L191) call `current_app.guarantee_blocking(...)` on the handler.
- `Quill.guarantee_blocking` (`src/quill/app.py:966`) returns plain `def` functions unchanged. For `async def` functions it wraps them with `nonblocking_to_blocking`, which runs the coroutine and waits for the result, so WSGI workers stay synchronous.
- A `VerbPage` subclass can therefore declare `async def get(self)` directly. There is no need for an async dispatch base class.

**Why this design makes sense:** sync and async views share one dispatch path (method lookup, `methods` computation, HEAD-to-GET fallback, `init_every_request`, decorators). A single adapter hook in the app decides how a coroutine gets run, and the docstring says to override it to change that. This mirrors Flask's `ensure_sync`. A parallel async class would duplicate the dispatch logic.

I read `views.py` and the `guarantee_blocking` definition only. I did not read the body of `nonblocking_to_blocking`.
